title: Design System: Food Label Health Agent

motion.name: proof-settle
motion.purpose: Uploaded proof settles into the workbench.

components.name: Correction Field
components.description: Editable OCR field with visible recovery state.
components.css: .ds-field{display:grid;gap:7px;color:#17201B;font:600 12px SFMono-Regular,monospace}.ds-field textarea{min-height:92px;border:1px solid #CDD4CE;border-radius:10px;padding:13px 14px;color:#17201B;background:#fff;font:450 16px/1.6 Avenir Next,sans-serif}.ds-field textarea:focus{outline:3px solid #D9E5FF;border-color:#185ADB}

components.name: Caution State
components.description: Uncertainty shown with label and symbol.

narrative.overview: A label is treated as a proof to inspect, annotate, confirm, and release—not as a lifestyle image to score.
keyCharacteristics: One dominant proofing workspace rather than a dashboard of equal cards.
Field confidence and source metadata use measurement typography.
Risk states always combine icon, label, and explanatory text.
Controls are compact, tactile, and familiar enough for one-handed mobile use.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Orange, amber, red, and green appear only when the interface can name the state they encode.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace communicates measurement or provenance; it never acts as a generic technical costume.

rules.name: The Single Lift Rule
rules.body: At most one large surface appears physically lifted in a viewport.

dos: Do show the label image beside the text the user is confirming.
Do put critical uncertainty before ingredient education or product recommendations.
Do keep source, date, confidence, and rule identity readable but visually secondary.
donts: Don't assign an absolute health score or imply medical clearance.
Don't use green alone to mean safe.
Don't structure the application as a grid of generic metric cards.
